subject: Clarifying spend safeguards, auto-pause options, and credit scenarios
messages:
From: Jamie Li <jamie@skyward.ai>
To: alex_martinez@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-03-22T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Overage behavior — what happens if we blow past our monthly budget?

Hi Alex,

Quick question from our FP&A team as we finalize the Q2 commit: if usage goes above the committed budget (either by accident or due to a burst), what does Redwood do automatically? Specifically:
- Will you pause the API or throttle?
- Do we get alerted and have to approve extra spend?
- Are there credits/refunds for accidental overages?
- Any paperwork/procurement steps we should prep (DocuSign, PO)?

We’re trying to lock an internal guardrail so we don’t surprise execs. Hope this is a quick one — thanks.

—Jamie
Jamie Li
Head of ML Ops, Skyward AI
jamie@skyward.ai

From: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.ai>
To: Jamie Li <jamie@skyward.ai>
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-03-22T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Overage behavior — what happens if we blow past our monthly budget?

Hi Jamie — great question, thanks for flagging. Short answer: you pick the behavior you'd like; we support a few guardrail modes. I attached our current rate card and a short cap template for the procurement team.

High-level options we offer for Hosted API customers (can be configured per-account):

1) Soft cap (recommended for trial-to-prod):
   - Alerting at 80%/90%/100% via email and webhooks; calls continue to flow.
   - We will attempt to contact the account owner for explicit approval of continued spend.
   - After 72 hours of sustained overage with no approval, requests are throttled to a reduced QPS until usage falls under the cap.

2) Hard pause (strict budget control):
   - At the threshold you define the platform automatically pauses new requests.
   - Existing in-flight tokens finish; new token generation is blocked.
   - Account owner must acknowledge or request a temporary uplift (true-up) to resume.

3) Auto-bill (for enterprise with credit acceptance):
   - Automatically bill overage at the contract’s overage rate.
   - Optional pre-approved spend increase can be set so small bursts are covered without manual approval.

About credits/refunds: we do not issue automatic refunds for usage billed under the normal contract. For clear platform issues (e.g., a bug in our routing that caused duplicate generations) we’ll investigate and, where appropriate, provide prorated credits. Accidental usage by a customer is typically handled via a one-time goodwill credit only at the discretion of our finance team and for qualifying cases.

I’ve looped in Neha (AM) who can outline operational defaults for hosted customers and Marissa (billing) for the formal finance options. If you can tell us which mode procurement prefers, we’ll draft the exact language for DocuSign/PO.

Attachments: redwood_rate_card_q1_2026.pdf, proposed_mop_cap_template.xlsx

Best,
Alex Martinez
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
alex_martinez@redwood.ai
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Jamie Li <jamie@skyward.ai>, alex_martinez@redwood.ai
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-03-22T15:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Overage behavior — operational defaults for hosted API

Hi Jamie — quick operational notes to supplement Alex’s overview: 

- Metering is near-real-time and billed at token granularity; throttles happen at the serving layer but billing is on actual tokens consumed.
- For Hosted API, our default (unless you contract otherwise) is a soft cap with 3 progressive alerts. We only enforce a hard pause if a hard cap is requested on the account.
- If you choose soft cap + auto-bill, we recommend a pre-approved uplift limit (e.g., 20% of committed spend) to avoid critical production interruptions. Anything above that requires an explicit approval flow that can be signed off by procurement or an API call from a designated admin.
- For high-risk workloads (streaming RLHF loops, unattended batch runs), we advise a hard cap in front of a staging project to avoid runaway spend.

If helpful, we can pre-populate the cap template with SKW-4379 baseline numbers and a few scenarios (conservative, normal, burst). Rishi — tagging you for any notes on negotiated overage rates we’ve discussed in other deals.

Neha Kapoor
Account Manager, Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
From: Jamie Li <jamie@skyward.ai>
To: alex_martinez@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@skyward.ai
Date: 2026-03-23T11:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Overage behavior — operational defaults for hosted API

Thanks Alex/Neha — that helps a lot. Two quick scenarios from procurement/FP&A: 

Scenario A (procurement prefers): hard pause at the exact monthly budget; we want zero surprise spend. If we hit it, pause and require a signed uptick.
Scenario B (platform team prefers): soft cap + auto-bill for bursts up to 25% (we’ll accept a predictable overage rate).

Follow-ups:
- If we choose hard pause, is there a material risk of customer-facing downtime we need to mitigate?
- If we choose auto-bill, procurement wants the DocuSign clause and a short sample clause describing the overage rate and pre-approved uplift.
- Are there SLAs tied to throttled vs paused behavior?

Procurement asked us to get a formal proposal so they can present to legal. Can Marissa/Billing supply the finance wording and the DocuSign-ready clause?

—Jamie
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jamie Li <jamie@skyward.ai>, alex_martinez@redwood.ai
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-03-24T17:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Overage behavior — formal options and DocuSign language

Hi Jamie — thanks for laying out the scenarios. Below are three clean options we can include in the SOW/DocuSign: please pick the letter that best matches procurement’s preference and we’ll produce a final SOW.

Option 1 — Strict hard cap (no-auto-bill):
  - Behavior: At the defined monthly threshold, the account’s generation endpoint is paused for new requests. In-flight requests are allowed to complete.
  - Admin flow: Admin must submit a signed request (DocuSign) or use the portal to request a temporary uplift.
  - SLA note: Redwood cannot guarantee uninterrupted service if the account elects this behavior; SLA credits apply only to platform incidents, not to customer-initiated pauses.

Option 2 — Soft cap + auto-bill (recommended for production with burst risk):
  - Behavior: Alerts at 80/90/100%; up to pre-approved uplift (customer-defined % or $) is automatically billed at the contract’s overage rate. If usage exceeds pre-approved uplift, calls are throttled; a second approval is required to continue.
  - Admin flow: Procurement signs the overage clause in DocuSign providing the pre-approved uplift amount.
  - Finance: Overage invoiced on next billing cycle; we can include an itemized overage report for reconciliation.

Option 3 — Rolling cap + negotiated overage rate (enterprise):
  - Behavior: Weekly rolling cap to smooth spikes; any sustained growth above baseline triggers a negotiated true-up rate.
  - Admin flow: Typically used by larger customers with committed capacity and custom metering.

Credits/refunds: as Alex noted, credits are only issued for platform faults. Goodwill credits for accidental usage are handled case-by-case and require Finance approval.

DocuSign language (sample clause):
  "Customer authorizes Redwood Inference to automatically bill overage consumption up to X% above the committed monthly spend at the overage rate of $Y per 1k tokens. Any consumption above the pre-approved uplift will require customer’s explicit approval before continued service. Customer may elect a hard cap instead, which will pause new token generation at the specified threshold."

Next steps: if you pick 1/2/3 we’ll: (a) fill the cap template with SKW-4379 numbers, (b) attach the clause to DocuSign, (c) route to procurement for signature.

I’ve attached the current rate card (same as Alex) and export of the cap template populated with conservative numbers — please review.

Best regards,
Marissa Cole
Senior Manager, Billing & Revenue Operations
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Attachments: redwood_rate_card_q1_2026.pdf, proposed_mop_cap_template.xlsx
